model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the relationship between accuracy (ACC, in percentage) and co-occurrence number for five different methods: Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROMЕ. The x-axis, labeled "Co-occurrence Number," is presented on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, with tick marks at 10^0, 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis, labeled "ACC (%)", is linear and ranges from 40 to 65. The "Base" method (black line with circles) shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 39% to 44% as the co-occurrence number increases. The "MEND" method (brown line with triangles) starts at about 44% and rises to approximately 56%. The "FT" method (blue line with triangles) begins at around 40% and increases to about 48%. The "MEMIT" method (purple line with circles) starts at 43% and climbs to 55%. The "ROMЕ" method (green line with squares) shows the highest accuracy, starting at 51% and increasing to 66%. All methods exhibit a general upward trend in accuracy with increasing co-occurrence number.
